page: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-3xL40S is a GPU-accelerated virtual server configured with 16 vCPUs and 192 GB of system memory, running on the KVM hypervisor. The processing power is delivered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor using the x86_64 architecture, featuring 16 physical cores with one thread per core on a shared CPU allocation model. Acceleration is provided by three NVIDIA L40S GPUs from the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering a combined 144 GB of VRAM. This instance does not include local storage.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-core CPU performance, with Geekbench single-core scores and stress-ng single-core metrics placing in the top 10%. Multi-core performance is strong, ranking in the top 25%. Memory performance is characterized by top-tier large-block write bandwidth of 203.06 GB/sec and strong read bandwidth. In LLM inference benchmarks, the system achieves top-tier performance for both prompt processing and text generation using small and medium models, processing 6015.0 tokens per second for medium model prompts.

Given the shared CPU allocation and the absence of local storage, this server type offers a specialized hardware profile that prioritizes high-density GPU resources over dedicated CPU cores. This makes it a qualitatively cost-effective option for workloads that are heavily dependent on GPU acceleration rather than sustained, exclusive CPU execution. Recommended workloads include large language model inference, image processing, and parallelized data science tasks that leverage the 144 GB of total VRAM.
